column1: # Provisional game profile (generated by scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py from the survey with dm/games/profile_guess.py, not checked by hand)
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# ---- NVN driver constant segments (Mario's values, the translator's built-in layout, unless the engine says otherwise) ----
# measured over all 854 shaders: texture handles (separate and combined) from c2+0x168 (17 offsets up to 0x560), samplers from 0x568, images from 0x120
# (the guess copied SDK 8's 0x20 / 32, and 1,149 texture bindings had no slot)
# the shaders are bare control section + code area pairs in shaders.nx (4A Engine), no BNSH container
# convert only the vertices each draw reads: the world sits in one vertex buffer of 6.2 million vertices with an 8/16-bit integer attribute the replay converts on the CPU, so converting the whole
# bound range overran the per-frame staging and the world draws were skipped (a dark, flat scene with no first-person weapon); per draw it is about 50,000 vertices a submission
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): one frame per display tick whatever interval the game asks for. 4A's engine steps its logic by real time: walking forward for 4 s ended at the same spot at 30 and at
# 60 fps (Mac, the prologue). The GPU needs about 3 ms a frame either way. DM_PRESENT_INTERVAL=game (Documents/env.txt) brings back the original 30
